rows.source: OPSS e-bike lithium-ion battery safety
rows.verified: The General Product Safety Regulations apply to e-bike lithium-ion batteries, including online sales and conversion kits, and unsafe batteries must not be placed on the market.

rows.source: OPSS e-bike lithium-ion battery safety
rows.verified: Thermal runaway occurs when cell reactions generate heat faster than it can dissipate, producing gases that can rupture the cell and cause fire or explosion.

rows.source: OPSS e-bike lithium-ion battery safety
rows.verified: Thermal runaway can heat adjacent cells and create a rapid cascading event through the battery pack.

rows.source: OPSS e-bike lithium-ion battery safety
rows.verified: A safe e-bike battery needs effective safety mechanisms, such as a battery management system, to prevent thermal runaway during normal use and foreseeable misuse.

rows.source: OPSS e-bike lithium-ion battery safety
rows.verified: The protection system should detect individual-cell voltage, pack current and cell temperature and act against unsafe voltage, current or temperature conditions.

rows.source: OPSS e-bike lithium-ion battery safety
rows.verified: Battery protection should prevent an incompatible charger from driving cells into thermal runaway.

rows.source: OPSS e-bike lithium-ion battery safety
rows.verified: Battery design should resist foreseeable temperature, liquid, impact and vibration damage and provide charger-compatibility and safe-charging information.

rows.source: OPSS e-bike lithium-ion battery safety
rows.verified: OPSS advises buying from a known seller, following instructions, using the recommended charger, charging without blocking exits, unplugging after charging and never modifying the battery.

rows.source: OPSS e-bike lithium-ion battery safety
rows.verified: E-bike battery risk depends on cell quality, design, BMS performance, charger compatibility, damage, charging behaviour, environment and foreseeable misuse.

rows.source: OPSS e-bike lithium-ion battery safety
rows.verified: OPSS battery evidence is product-, charger-, use-, damage-, environment-, control- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level fire probability.

rows.source: CAA Drone and Model Aircraft Code
rows.verified: The remote pilot is responsible for safe flying, must be ready for failures and may face fines or imprisonment for serious legal breaches.

rows.source: CAA Drone and Model Aircraft Code
rows.verified: The aircraft must remain in direct sight with a full view of surrounding airspace, without binoculars, telephoto lenses or electronic viewing equipment.

rows.source: CAA Drone and Model Aircraft Code
rows.verified: An observer must stand next to the pilot, maintain communication and help keep direct sight, while the pilot remains responsible for safety.

rows.source: CAA Drone and Model Aircraft Code
rows.verified: First-person-view flying requires an observer and compliance with the observer rules.

rows.source: CAA Drone and Model Aircraft Code
rows.verified: For applicable aircraft categories, a minimum 50 metre horizontal distance from uninvolved people applies and the aircraft must not fly over that no-fly cylinder.

rows.source: CAA Drone and Model Aircraft Code
rows.verified: Drones must never be flown over crowds, regardless of aircraft size.

rows.source: CAA Drone and Model Aircraft Code
rows.verified: Pilots must stay outside flight restriction zones without permission and verify current restrictions because onboard software or apps may be incomplete or outdated.

rows.source: CAA Drone and Model Aircraft Code
rows.verified: Pilots must not hinder emergency services and must safely stop flying near an incident unless permission is given; flying outside the Code requires the correct authorisation.

rows.source: CAA Drone and Model Aircraft Code
rows.verified: Drone risk depends on aircraft weight and class, operating category, people, location, weather, speed, airspace restrictions and authorisation.

rows.source: CAA Drone and Model Aircraft Code
rows.verified: CAA Drone Code evidence is aircraft-, pilot-, operation-, location-, weather-, authorisation- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level incident probability.
